note: SIXTH SPP KEEPER, PROMOTED 2026-09-10 (lane SPP-61) over keeper 5 (lane SPP-52a) BY OWNER RULING in-session, verbatim: 'Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote... If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper.' THE RUN: keeper 5's recipe plus EXACTLY ONE change -- ScenarioConfig.eia860_vintage_tracks_solve_year armed true through the registered --set channel on replay_keeper.py. ZERO code change, zero shared default flipped, zero new tunable. Solved as ONE --years 2023 2024 2025 invocation, years sequential (rules 12 / 16 [R-ALLYEARS]), 655 s wall. THIS IS THE FIRST ARM OF eia860_vintage_tracks_solve_year IN ANY COMMITTED RUN, IN ANY ISO. WHY IT IS THE KEEPER -- AND IT IS NOT BECAUSE IT SCORES BETTER, BECAUSE IT DOES NOT. Unarmed, load_fleet_from_csv resolves every backcast year against the canonical EIA-860 2025 Early Release snapshot, so keeper 5's 2023 and 2024 fleets carry a fuel vintage and a unit population those years did not have. Measured registry totals, control: 60,749.0 / 60,739.9 / 60,739.9 MW across three years -- a fleet that barely evolves, which is precisely the pjm-167 defect this field was built for. Armed: -2,715.4 MW in 2023 and -3,175.3 MW in 2024, restoring real annual evolution. Harrington 6193 lands exactly on its own vintage (2023 1,018.0 MW all COAL; 2024 679.0 MW COAL + 339.0 MW ST_GAS; 2025 unchanged at 1,018.0 MW ST_GAS, correctly, the units having converted Feb/Mar/Jun 2025). The footprint is deliberately NOT confined to plant 6193 and the lane's PRECOMMIT said so before the solve: the three largest non-Harrington 2023 moves are CT_PEAKER plants 64547 (-442.2 MW, absent entirely), 64548 (-151.2 MW, absent entirely) and 57881 (763.0 -> 232.8 MW) -- units that DID NOT EXIST in 2023 and are correctly absent from the 2023 release. The wider footprint is the vintage being right, not the vintage being broken. The promotion rests on rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] ('never revert to an estimate just because it fits the backcast better') and rule 1 [R-STRUCT] ('a run is a keeper because it is the most structurally faithful, not because it has the lowest MAE'). THE GATED FIT GETS WORSE AND THE REPAIR STAYS IN -- REPORTED AT FULL MAGNITUDE, NEVER ABSORBED. C1 fuel-mix goes from ONE failing row to TWO. Keeper 5: 2024 ST_GAS -8.13 TWh, with 2023 passing on 1.05 TWh of headroom. This run: 2023 ST_GAS -8.38 TWh (share -2.9 pp) AND 2024 ST_GAS -9.71 TWh (share -3.3 pp), both out of band. The lane's PRECOMMIT §4 named this exact risk before the solve -- '2023 is at real risk and this lane may break it' -- and pre-committed to keeping the repair either way. KEEPER 5'S NOTE BET THE OPPOSITE: it named this row 'the highest-value next lever' and projected that repairing it would leave C3c the LONE failure and make SPP read CALIBRATED under rule 22 [R-C3C]. THAT BET IS MEASURED AND LOST, and the loss is recorded here rather than quietly dropped. Half of it was already falsified at ZERO LP by this lane's phase 0: the charter's two-sided premise claimed the EIA-923 benchmark books Harrington's coal under ST_GAS, and it does not -- the bench frame is completely inert to the EIA-860 vintage (0 klass rows differing by >1 MWh in all three years) and already books the plant's coal as COAL_PRB (3.1775 / 2.0590 / 0.0000 TWh). There was never a bench-side repair to make. WHAT THE DEGRADATION ACTUALLY DIAGNOSES -- root-caused, not buried (rule 14). Model ST_GAS was ALREADY 6.95 / 8.13 TWh BELOW actual before the arm. The arm removes 744.5 / 948.4 MW of ST_GAS and 1,308.0 / 1,282.1 MW of CT_PEAKER capacity that did not exist in those years, which removes a COMPENSATING ERROR rather than creating a new one: the too-large canonical fleet had been partially masking a gas-steam merit-order shortfall. The residual is an ST_GAS offer / commitment defect, NOT a fleet-vintage defect, and it is the named successor object for the next SPP lane. THE FULL SCORED COMPARISON, both runs re-scored by scripts/calibration_verdict.py on the same bench: DETERMINATION NOT-YET on both, and on the IDENTICAL basis (fuelmix, price_tail). C1 FAIL -> FAIL (1 row -> 2 rows, WORSE). C2 system volume PASS -> PASS. C3a mean LMP PASS -> PASS. C3b price duration/shape PASS -> PASS. C3c price tail FAIL -> FAIL (model 0/4/2 h above $200 -> 0/5/0 h, against 42/59/68 actual). C4 PASS -> PASS. C6 governance PASS -> PASS. C8 forced-energy share PASS -> PASS. C5a CO2 (REPORTED-ONLY, rubric v2.9, contributes no status) -2.6 / -2.0 / +3.0 % -> -5.6 / -3.1 / +2.9 %, WORSE, reported at full magnitude and routed with the same ST_GAS shortfall. D-10 free-class C1 15/16 all · 11/12 free -> 14/16 all · 10/12 free. WHAT IMPROVES BESIDES THE FLEET: the REPORTED-ONLY D-A diurnal amplitude rises in the two complete-bench years, 36.9 / 35.2 % of measured -> 38.5 / 38.1 %, recovering most of the ~2 pp keeper 5's level cut had cost; and 2025 diurnal PHASE repairs from OFF to OK (peak h12 vs h17 -> h17 vs h17, hod r +0.879 -> +0.893). 2025 amplitude falls 28.9 -> 24.3 %, reported. THE PRE-REGISTERED STRUCTURAL SCREEN CLEARED (rule 29 [R-SCREEN]). Screen year 2023, named in the PRECOMMIT before the solve by MEASURED FOOTPRINT (Harrington reclassified capacity 1,018.0 MW vs 679.0; measured coal 3.1775 vs 2.0590 TWh) and deliberately NOT the residual year, which is 2024. G3 dispatch response: coal family +2.8178 TWh against a pre-registered band of +1.0 to +4.5 TWh, and ST_GAS falls rather than rises (8.3546 -> 7.0867 TWh), both as required. G4: no non-target load-bearing criterion flips PASS -> FAIL (C2 / C3a / C3b all still PASS). G1 / G2 / G5 were established at phase 0. C1's residual is read NOWHERE in the gate, by design. RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: armed PER RUN through --set on SPP's own bundle. The dataclass default stays False and is registered in _CACHE_KEY_OPTIONAL_FIELDS at that declared value, so every pre-existing cache key of all seven ISOs is byte-stable, no ISOConfig.default_scenario_overrides is touched, and no other ISO moves. No fitted number crosses an ISO boundary; the arm derives entirely from SPP's own committed EIA-860 releases. The same repair is presumptively owed in every other ISO on rule-14 grounds -- ROUTED, not transferred: each ISO's desk owns that decision on its own measurement (rule 28(d)), and every other ISO's cell enters as U. RULE 21 [R-DOF]: the DOF ledger is INHERITED VERBATIM from keeper 5 -- n_entries 3, n_residual 2, unchanged -- because eia860_vintage_tracks_solve_year is a GATED bool with no tunable scalar, identified by the EIA-860 annual releases themselves. It is declared in the attestation's measured_input_switches block. Keeper 5's authorized_price_tuning block (offer_curve_by_group 0.93 on all four bands of the ten registered fossil classes, rules 1 / 13 amendment 2026-09-05) carries over unchanged and still PASSES C6. ONE LATENT DEFECT FOUND AND ROUTED, NOT TOUCHED: in scripts/run_calibration_full.py the benchmark's group_by_code is built BEFORE run_year sets the year's vintage, so under an armed run the bench bucket reads the previous year's vintage. Measured effect for SPP: EXACTLY ZERO (the bench frame is inert to the vintage in all three years). Repairing an inert shared driver outside this lane's object would be an unmeasured change; routed to the desk register for the ISOs where the CAMPD backfill does fire. WHAT THIS KEEPER DOES NOT FIX, stated so no reader infers otherwise: SPP is NOT calibrated and this promotion does not move it closer on the scoreboard -- it moves it closer on the fleet. C1's ST_GAS rows and C3c's absent price tail are both still open, SPP still has NO scarcity mechanism of any kind (SPP-55/56's object), and keeper 5's other named structural objects are ALL still open and NOT closed here: the thermal-commitment floor (the LP absorbs 98.2 % of the concentrated curtailment headroom by turning thermal down to an annual minimum of 254.3 MW across a ~40 GW fleet) and the zonal spread (measured |N-S| 12.13 / 17.23 / 15.18 against a model ~1). INHERITED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: the vre_curtailment_oversupply_allocation mechanism and the actual-LMP CLOCK REPAIR (every SPP C3a / C3b number older than 2026-09-09 is on the unrepaired clock and is NOT comparable to these). Control for every later SPP lane = THIS bundle (rule 29(b) form 4); its hourly/ sidecars are COMMITTED so a later lane differences against it without a re-solve. G-DRIFT at promotion: zero solve-path hunks between the solve's pinned base and origin/main (src/market_sim, scripts/lib, config and the calibration runners all unchanged; the only diffs were two MISO-lane _validation-source artifacts, INERT for SPP). LINEAGE: SPP-40 -> SPP-42 -> SPP-43 (keeper 3) -> SPP-51c (keeper 4) -> SPP-52a (keeper 5) -> this run.
